rows.evidence: catalog-record-codecs.ts:223 rejects a baseline only when the recomputed digest differs (or is null). The only writers are catalog-service: adopt computes the digest over the same content at :518 and commits baseline+catalog+pointer in one commit at :550-552; revise clones the parsed content and recomputes at :695, committing :728-730. grep over src for BASELINE_SCHEMA_ID / ArchitectureBaselineRevisionSnapshot@1 finds no other writer (plan-readers.ts:324 only registers a validator that checks the digest's shape, not its match, but no production commit uses that schema outside catalog-service, and commitRaw has no src caller). The other snapshot readers consume stored rows/events (evidence-service.ts:515, codec :445, :502). Writing a mismatched digest needs the test-only raw seed; the pre-T tests that reached it used commitRaw tampering (before/tests/helpers/graph-session-fixture.ts:421-431; before/tests/work-graph/A1-architecture-catalog.test.ts:184-187), removed by TQ-105/TQ-110 for tamper.
rows.proposal_note: Keep. Both propose no tamper test; nothing else performs the read-side digest check on the current-pointer path, so deleting it would let a damaged body be trusted beside valid pins.

rows.evidence: catalog-record-codecs.ts:402 rejects a stored row whose since is non-null and not ^c\d{10}$. Writers always write null at catalog-service.ts:524 (adopt) and :702 (revise); the revise commit fills the placeholder with the real commit cursor through commitCursorBindings at :736, and the store binds before writing and re-validates the bound row (sqlite-record-store.ts:455, record-codec.ts:619 and :730-740). T made the key mandatory (:396 exactKeys), so even an old row without since now fails earlier, not this arm. A non-cursor since therefore means a hand-edited/corrupt row; no other writer of this schema exists.
rows.proposal_note: Keep untested. The check is part of the registered validator (codecs:518-520) that runs on commit and on decode reads (:562); it is the read-side mapping of a damaged row to unavailable, so there is nothing to delete and no public step or seam produces the shape (rule 4).

rows.evidence: catalog-record-codecs.ts:459 is only reached through validateArchitectureCatalogRevisedEvent (:511; grep shows no other caller of readArchitectureCatalogRecordValue). The revised event embeds catalogRecord with since:null (catalog-service.ts:702, event built :707-711); only the stored record's since is bound (:736), never the event payload, and restoreRevised:327-330 documents that the embedded since is the pre-bind null placeholder while the cursor is supplied only to the returned value. A non-null since in the event therefore needs a hand-edited/corrupt event; no platform writer emits it.
rows.proposal_note: Keep the reject. The proposed simplification to `since !== null` is sound: the event payload is never bound, so even a well-formed cursor string would be wrong there, and the helper has no other caller.

rows.evidence: catalog-service.ts:392-393 returns unavailable only when readArchitectureBaselineSnapshot rejects the stored row. readCurrentCatalogWindow reads pointer, baseline and catalog together in one readMany (:379) after re-checking the pointer (:382-389), and both writers commit all three rows in one transaction (:550-552, :728-730), so a concurrent revise becomes source_stale before :393 and cannot split pointer from baseline. A damaged or digest-inconsistent row needs a hand-edited or old-format store (TQ-105; decision 79 drops old formats); pre-T the arm was reached only by the commitRaw tamper seed (before/tests/work-graph/A1-architecture-catalog.test.ts:184-187, before/tests/work-graph/A1-session-lifecycle.test.ts:112-120).
rows.proposal_note: Keep. Both propose no tamper test; it is the current-pointer read's only refusal of a damaged baseline, and no other layer rejects it before this read.

rows.evidence: catalog-service.ts:395-396. Baseline, catalog and active pointer are written only in catalog-service and always in one commit (:548-552 adopt, :726-730 revise); grep for activeRefKey / ProjectArchitectureBaselineActive finds no other writer, and the pointer is re-verified at :382-389 after the batch read. A missing catalog beside a live pointer therefore means an old-format (pre-8A, decision 79) or hand-edited store. The guard cannot simply be dropped: decodeArchitectureCatalogRecord(undefined) would throw because validateArchitectureCatalog dereferences record.schemaId at codec:395.
rows.proposal_note: Keep untested. 'Merge into the damaged branch at :399' can only mean both outcomes are unavailable; an explicit undefined check is still needed to avoid the TypeError, so the arm stays (rule 4).
